Thanks Samir  good to have Aaron looped in. Quick answers and an initial estimate attached.

Streaming vs batch (short answer)
- Streaming + small batch size is typically best for very latency-sensitive interactive flows (<=300ms p95). It reduces tail latency because requests are processed as they arrive instead of queuing.
- That approach has a modest cost premium vs aggressive batching (we typically see a 1540% delta depending on model and request distribution).

Initial pricing scenarios (high level)  see attached spreadsheet for details: 
- Hosted Standard (cost-focused): $700  $1,100 / 1M tokens, estimated 500ms p95 for interactive flows with medium batching.
- Hosted Streaming-optimized: $900  $1,400 / 1M tokens, target ~250350ms p95 for interactive flows (depends on model and avg tokens).
- Dedicated Reserved (Committed capacity): equivalent unit cost can be ~3050% lower at scale for sustained volumes (50M+/mo), plus predictable latency (we can provision for <250ms p95).

Suggested next steps
1) Tech deep-dive w/ Monica to validate model choice + batching/streaming config (3045 min).
2) We'll deliver a short TCO for the three scenarios showing projected monthly spend at 50M / 100M / 200M tokens.
3) Share a draft SOW and procurement checklist for your security team. [Attachment: pricing-model.xlsx, SOW_draft.pdf]

Hi Samir / Marissa  Monica from Solutions here, quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive.

Latency vs cost: practical levers
- Streaming + small batch (14 reqs): best for p95 < 300ms but you trade throughput efficiency. Expect ~2040% higher $/1M tokens vs large batching for the same model.
- Batching (1050 reqs): great for throughput/price; p95 increases with queueing. Good for background summarization.
- KV/prefix caching: for repeated prompts or few-shot patterns, caching can reduce token generation and cut billable tokens by 1030%.
- Quantization & model-family selection: Llama 3 13B with 4-bit quantization gives big cost wins with modest quality loss in many prompt types  we can test.

SLO-driven routing idea (what we can implement)
- Tier A (latency-critical): streaming nodes, reserved capacity, priority SLA  price premium ~+30% over base hosted.
- Tier B (balanced): hosted standard with medium batching  base price.
- Tier C (cost-optimized): background workers, large batching, spot-scale  up to -40% unit price.

Estimated unit economics (very rough, to be validated in TCO sheet)
- Base hosted: ~$1,000 / 1M tokens (model dependent)
- Streaming-opt: ~$1,300 / 1M tokens (for target p95 ~250300ms)
- Dedicated w/ commitments: ~$600  $900 / 1M tokens at sustained 50M+ volumes

I'll bring sample latency curves and recommended batch-size profiles to Tue's call. Also, if you can share 23 representative request traces (anonymized), we can run a quick sim.

Thanks  looking forward to the deep-dive.
